name: CVSO 30

planets.name: b
planets.note: Short-period (0.4484 d) transiting/RV candidate (PTFO 8-8695 b); by ~2020-2021 the fading-event phase had drifted far from precession-model predictions and TESS photometry was better explained by starspot modulation than by transits, casting strong doubt on the planetary interpretation.

planets.name: c
planets.note: Wide-separation (1.85"/662 au) direct-imaging candidate reported by Schmidt et al. 2016; Lee & Chiang (2017) showed its optical/IR colors and brightness are inconsistent with a substellar object and are instead consistent with a background K-type giant or M subdwarf contaminant.

extra_papers.title: Evidence that the Planetary Candidate CVSO30c is a Background Star from Optical, Seeing-limited Data

images.wavelength_label: JHK band (Dec 2012 epoch); candidate c at 1.85" separation

paper.title: Direct Imaging discovery of a second planet candidate around the possibly transiting planet host CVSO 30

notes: Both reported companions are now considered dubious/refuted: c is most likely a background star (Lee & Chiang 2017), and b's transit signal is likely stellar starspot activity rather than a planet (Koen 2020, MNRAS 494, 4349; Koen 2021, A&A 647, L1 -- no arXiv preprints available for these two).
